title: Routing Basics
description: Understand how routing works in ASP.NET Core.

data.text: **Routing** maps HTTP requests to controller actions. ASP.NET Core supports convention-based and attribute routing.

data.caption: An incoming HTTP request is matched against a route, then forwarded to the controller action.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
  A[Incoming HTTP Request] --> B{Route Table Match}
  B -->|Convention| C[Convention Router]
  B -->|Attribute| D[Attribute Router]
  C --> E[Controller Action]
  D --> E
  E --> F[Result: JSON / View / StatusCode]

data.text: Convention-based routing uses a pattern to map URLs to controllers and actions. It is configured once in `Program.cs` and applies to all routes unless overridden.

data.title: Convention

data.text: Attribute routing declares routes directly on controllers and actions using attributes. It gives you explicit control over every URL and is the preferred approach for web APIs.

data.title: Attribute

cards.title: Convention Routing
cards.description: Centralized pattern-based routing configured in Program.cs.

cards.title: Attribute Routing
cards.description: Routes declared directly on controllers and actions.

terms.definition: The process of matching incoming HTTP requests to controller actions.
Routing driven by a central pattern configured in Program.cs.
Routing declared directly on controllers and actions using attributes.

data.title: API Routing
data.text: Web APIs typically use attribute routing for explicit control over URLs.

data.title: Map the Route
data.description: Given the route pattern below, predict which controller action handles each URL.
steps: Look at the [Route] prefix on the controller
Match the HTTP method attribute ([HttpGet], [HttpPost], etc.)
Substitute route tokens with the URL segments
data.expectedOutcome: Correctly identify that /api/products/10 maps to ProductsController.Get(10).

items.text: Understand that routing maps URLs to actions
items.hint: Routing is the entry point of every request.
Uses a single pattern in Program.cs.
Explicit routes are clearer for HTTP endpoints.
Tokens are replaced with the controller name minus 'Controller'.
